memory_candidates.content: BimodalLogic's update-task-status.sh has no flag or code path that sets a free-text `blockers` field on a task record -- its only state-mutating flags are --file-scope-add, --research-questions, --hold-reason, --depends-on-add. hold_reason is a [HOLD]-specific triad (hold_reason/held_at/prior_status), not a general blocker annotation. Tasks with a populated free-text `blockers` field (298, 428, 257, 481) were set by a direct state.json edit, not through this script, and this is independent of a task's `status` value -- task 298 is status=partial with a populated prose blockers field, so 'partial' does not preclude a blockers entry.

In BimodalLogic, state.json's `roadmap_batches` array (maintained by /roadmap, a separate periodic maintenance pass distinct from any individual task's own lifecycle) can carry a batch rationale that is temporally more current than a task's own filed/AMENDED description, when /roadmap runs between the task's filing and its dispatch. When a task's research phase finds the two disagree, cross-check both against direct reads of the live files rather than trusting either source outright -- /roadmap is explicitly barred from writing specs/ROADMAP.md itself, so a roadmap_batches rationale can correctly identify that ROADMAP.md prose needs updating without that update having happened yet.
